title: Mid-Caps Outgrow Large-Caps in Q2 as Persistent Revenue Jumps 20%, TCS Profit Rises 15%
excerpt: Persistent Systems posted 20% dollar revenue growth and a 26th straight sequential rise in Q2 FY27, while TCS delivered 15% profit growth and Wipro's profit slipped — with Infosys still to report on October 23.
body:
• Mid-cap IT firms are outgrowing large-caps on revenue in Q2 FY27: Persistent Systems reported dollar revenue up 20.0% year on year to $487.6 million, its 26th straight sequential growth quarter.
  • Large-caps delivered steadier profit growth: TCS net profit rose 15% to Rs 13,884 crore on revenue up 11.2% to Rs 73,188 crore, while Wipro profit fell 1.4% despite revenue up 9.1%.
  • Infosys has not reported yet — its Q2 results are due Friday, October 23 — and investors are watching its guidance and AI revenue commentary most closely.
  • For diaspora investors holding Indian IT ADRs or Nifty IT funds, the trade-off is clear: mid-caps offer faster growth at premium valuations (Persistent trades near 46 times earnings), large-caps offer dividends and lower volatility.

India's IT earnings season has split into two races. The large-caps — Tata Consultancy Services, Infosys and Wipro — are posting steady, single-to-low-double-digit growth powered by scale and artificial intelligence deals. The mid-caps, led by Persistent Systems and Coforge, are growing revenue roughly twice as fast, albeit off a much smaller base and at far richer valuations.

The Large-Cap Scoreboard

TCS set the tone for the season. According to Finowings' summary of the Q2 FY27 results, TCS revenue rose 11.2% year on year to Rs 73,188 crore and net profit rose 15% to Rs 13,884 crore, with an operating margin of 24%. Its annualised AI revenue crossed $3.1 billion — more than 10% of total revenue — total contract value stood at $9.6 billion, and the company declared a second interim dividend of Rs 12 per share.

Wipro was the mixed large-cap story: revenue rose 9.1% to Rs 24,753 crore, but net profit slipped about 1.4% to Rs 3,201 crore, even as its IT services operating margin improved to 16.5%. Infosys, the second-largest firm, reports on October 23. Its chief executive Salil Parekh said this week that AI services, already over 8% of revenue, could account for 20-30% of the company's work within a few quarters and almost half in two to three years, according to Upstox.

Mid-Caps: Faster Growth, Different Risks

Persistent Systems is the clearest mid-cap evidence. In its official Q2 FY27 release, Persistent reported revenue of $487.6 million, up 7.8% sequentially and 20.0% year on year, with an EBIT margin of 15.0% and order bookings of $633.5 million in total contract value. In rupee terms revenue rose 30.3% to Rs 4,663.9 crore. The catch: reported net profit fell 25.4% to Rs 351.5 crore because of one-time expenses tied to its Nagarro acquisition, in which it has secured about 94.04% of share capital — a reminder that mid-cap growth currently comes with acquisition costs and margin pressure.

"We are pleased to report Q2 FY27 revenue of USD 487.6M, marking our 26th sequential quarter of growth."

— Sandeep Kalra, Chief Executive Officer, Persistent Systems

Coforge, the other mid-cap most often paired with Persistent, shares the same profile in the sector summaries: smaller, faster-growing, driven by large-deal ramp-ups and niche digital and AI work, with a higher-risk, higher-reward profile than the big five. Brokerage trackers have consistently shown Tier-II dollar revenue growth averaging roughly double the Tier-I average in recent quarters.

What the Market Is Pricing

The market rewarded the whole sector on October 21: the Nifty IT index rose 1.85% in a falling broader market, with Wipro up 3.24%, Infosys up 2.10%, TCS up 1.90%, Coforge up 1.45% and Persistent up 1.28% by early afternoon, according to NSE data reported by Upstox. Analysts cited encouraging Q2 earnings, healthy deal wins and partnerships with Nvidia, Anthropic and Google. Helios Capital's Samir Arora cautioned against treating Indian IT as an "anti-AI trade," warning that a fall in US equities would also hurt Indian markets.

What's Next

Infosys on October 23 is the next verdict on large-cap demand and guidance. After that, the question is whether mid-caps can convert faster revenue growth into profit growth once acquisition costs fade — and whether their premium multiples survive if large-cap AI revenue keeps compounding at TCS's pace.
